title: Preflight Evidence, SIEM Export & Exception Protocol
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working worksheet is intended to be the canonical preflight checklist for security evidence required for production releases that touch authentication, RBAC v2 changes, audit-logging schema updates, or SIEM export modifications. It is a practical runbook for engineers, SREs, and the security approvers to gather, validate, and submit evidence for launch sign-off or to request an exception.

Context / why this exists:
- We frequently ship small config and schema changes that still require a minimal security review.
- Past gaps: missed audit-field mapping for token-service, and a SIEM field rename that broke queries.
- Goal: reduce back-and-forth by providing a reproducible extraction + validation checklist and a clear exception approval flow.

Quick definitions (as used here):
- RBAC v2: the new role/permission model landing across control plane APIs.
- Evidence bundle: concrete artifacts (logs, screenshots, validated JSON schema, test queries) attached to an approval issue.
- SIEM export: the outbound pipeline transforming audit events to the external SIEM (fields mapping, normalization, timestamping).

Preflight checklist (run before marking release as ready for security sign-off):
1) Owner & scope
   - Document the release owner (engineering lead) and the surface area: services, APIs, and infra touched.
   - Minimal example: owner: @marcus, components: token-service, auth-gateway, auditstream.

2) RBAC v2 mapping verification
   - Attach mapping table: role -> allowed resources -> allowed actions (CSV or JSON).
   - Confirm backward compatibility tests: for each legacy role, run the compatibility matrix (script: /scripts/rbac/check_compat.sh).
   - Evidence to attach: mapping file, compatibility test run output (stdout log).

3) Audit log schema changes
   - List fields added/removed/renamed. For each field, note: event type, reason, consumer impact.
   - Provide sample raw event(s) (pre-change and post-change) as lines from production-like test stream (redact PII).
   - Validate schema with schema validator: /ops/audit-schema/validate.py --file sample_events.json. Attach validator output.

4) SIEM export configuration check
   - Export mapping doc: map "platform_event.field" -> "siem_field".
   - Verify timestamp format is RFC3339 and timezone normalized (UTC).
   - Run a dry-export against staging SIEM endpoint (or local simulator) and capture the result. Command example: curl -X POST $STAGING_SIEM_ENDPOINT -d @sample_event.json -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -v
   - Evidence: exported payloads, SIEM-simulator response, JSON diff vs expected.

5) Evidence automation runbook (how to produce the bundle)
   - Steps:
     a) Checkout release branch and note commit SHA.
     b) Run schema validator and store output to evidence/validator-output.txt.
     c) Run rbac compatibility script -> evidence/rbac-compat.log.
     d) Produce 3 sample events per changed event-type (anonymize) -> evidence/sample-events.json.
     e) Run dry SIEM export -> evidence/siem-dryrun.json + evidence/siem-response.txt.
     f) Capture a short traceroute/latency sample if export touches new region endpoints.

6) Regression smoke tests to include in bundle
   - Auth smoke: create token, call protected route, ensure 200 + expected audit event emitted.
   - Negative auth test: unauthorized call yields 403 and audit event with reason code.
   - RBAC boundary test: attempt action with reduced role, verify deny + audit record with role tag.
   - Attach test results with timestamps and commit SHAs.

7) Privacy & PII check
   - Ensure all sample events are redacted. Fields to strip: user.email, user_ssn, raw_request_body unless necessary (then redact).
   - Note whether KMS/HSM keys were involved in the change.

Sign-off matrix (who must sign based on change severity):
- Minor config change (no schema / no RBAC mapping change): Owner + Eng TL.
- RBAC mapping change only: Owner + Eng TL + Security Engineer.
- Audit schema or SIEM export change: Owner + Eng TL + Security Engineer + Observability Lead.
- Any PII-handling changes: above + Privacy Officer.

Exception approval flow (when you cannot provide full evidence by release):
1) Quick triage: Owner opens SEC-EXC-<incremental-id> with description, reason, and what evidence is missing.
2) Attach what you do have (partial evidence bundle) and proposed compensating controls (e.g., feature flag, limited rollout to internal org).
3) Security reviewer assigns a provisional approval with a hard deadline for remediation (e.g., must remediate within 14 days or roll back).
4) If request is high-risk, schedule 30-min rapid review with Security, Observability, and SRE.
5) Log final approval + remedial actions as comments on SEC-EXC ticket and link to release notes.

Minimum evidence bundle (for a standard approval):
- mapping.csv or mapping.json (RBAC)
- validator-output.txt (audit schema validation)
- sample-events.json (3 samples per changed event)
- siem-dryrun.json and siem-response.txt
- smoke-test-results.txt
- signoff checklist filled (this doc snippet)

Template checklist to paste into approval ticket:
- [ ] Owner + scope defined
- [ ] RBAC mapping attached
- [ ] Schema diff attached and validated
- [ ] Sample events attached (PII redacted)
- [ ] SIEM dry-run completed and attached
- [ ] Smoke tests passed
- [ ] Signoffs collected as per matrix

Common failure modes observed (notes from past incidents):
- Field renames in audit payloads break saved SIEM searches (fix: add aliasing in export mapping and communicate change).
- Timestamp rounding issues: some consumers expected millis, other micros. Standardize on RFC3339 + nanos in export.
- Missing role tags on audit events — causes inability to trace authorization decisions. Add instrumentation hooks in auth-gateway.

Open questions / designers notes:
- Should we introduce a version header in every audit event (audit_schema_version) to make consumer migrations easier? (posited: yes)
- Can we add automated gating in CI that performs a SIEM-dryrun for PRs that touch audit/export code? (worth exploring)

Useful commands & helpers (for engineers):
- Validate schema: python ops/audit-schema/validate.py --file evidence/sample-events.json
- RBAC compat: ./scripts/rbac/check_compat.sh --mapping mapping.json --output evidence/rbac-compat.log
- Create evidence bundle: tar czf evidence-bundle-<sha>.tgz evidence/*
- Create exception ticket template (use SEC-EXC in Jira) and paste minimal checklist above.

Attachments to include when you file for sign-off:
- evidence-bundle-<sha>.tgz (prefer S3 link)
- link to PR and commit SHAs
- test run IDs and logs
- screenshots of SIEM saved search queries affected (if any)

Reviewer tips (for security reviewers):
- Prioritize recently changed event types and fields consumed by critical alerts.
- Ask for the siem-dryrun.json first — seeing actual exported payloads quickly reveals mapping issues.
- Check RBAC mapping for wildcard permissions that may have been introduced accidentally.

Audit trail & recording expectations:
- All approvals and exception tickets must record the exact evidence bundle link (S3 or Artifact store) and the exact commit SHA.
- Security will append a short review summary to the SEC ticket and tag the release notes entry.

Changelog for this worksheet:
- 2024-11-05: initial draft (Anika)
- 2024-12-12: added SIEM dry-run examples and commands (Marcus)
- 2025-01-22: included RBAC compat script references (Priya)
- 2025-03-01: clarified sign-off matrix and exception SLA (security)

Unresolved / nice-to-have
- Auto-generation of the "minimum evidence bundle" from CI artifacts.
- A central UI widget in Console to attach evidence bundles to releases (instead of Jira links).

Notes to self:
- When redacting sample events, run tools/redact-event.py with --policy default before uploading.
- Keep the SIEM-simulator locally in tools/siem-sim for offline verification.

End of worksheet.

If anything in here is blocked or unclear, ping #sec-release on Slack and tag @anika for quick help.
